gallery.title: File:USS Bowfin SS 287 in drydock 2004.jpg
gallery.artist: United States Navy, Journalist Seaman Ryan C. McGinley
gallery.credit: Navy NewsStand Photo ID: 041005-N-3019M-001Navy NewsStand Home
gallery.description: Pearl Harbor, Hawaii (Oct. 5, 2004) — Marisco Ltd. workers repair the aging hull of the decommissioned Balao-class submarine USS Bowfin (SS-287) at their shipyard near the former Naval Air Station Barber's Point, during a restoration project. Bowfin has served as a floating museum for 23 years, and is moored next to the USS Arizona Memorial Visitor's Center. Known as the "Pearl Harbor Avenger," Bowfin was launched one year to the day after Dec. 7, 1941 and was credited with sinking 44 enemy ships during the course of her nine extraordinary war patrols.

gallery.title: File:Poseidon C-3 Missile1.jpg
gallery.credit: originally posted to Flickr as Poseidon C-3 Missile
gallery.description: The only one of its kind to be on public display, a Poseidon C-3 missile with all of its electronics, hydraulics and propulsion elements still intact, is on display for visitors to examine at USS Bowfin Submarine Museum & Park. This massive cutaway mock-up weighs 12,000 pounds, is 34 feet long and is 74 inches in diameter. The C-3 strategic missile was capable of being launched from a submerged Fleet Ballistic Missile submarine. The first submarine to carry and launch a C-3 missile was USS James Madison (SSBN-627) in August of 1970. The missile was donated to the Museum by the U.S. Navy through Lockheed Missiles and Space Company, which manufactured the C-3 missiles for the Navy. See also: en:UGM-73 Poseidon

gallery.title: File:USS Bowfin Officers Second Patrol.png
gallery.description: Officers of the American WWII submarine USS Bowfin (SS-287). Picture taken on December 9, 1943 at Fremantle Submarine Base after returning from Bowfin's second war patrol. Commanding officer Walter T. Griffith (third from right) is wearing a Navy Cross awarded to him pierside by Rear Admiral Ralph Waldo Christie. From left to right: LT Carl W. Adams, LCDR William C. Thompson, ENS John R. Bertrand, ENS C. P. "Herb" Hoover, LTJG John P. "Pat" Doherty, LCDR Walter T. Griffith, LT Davis Cone, LTJG Howard E. Clark.

gallery.filename: RADM Ralph W Christie and LCDR Walter T Griffith on USS Bowfin.png
gallery.title: File:RADM Ralph W Christie and LCDR Walter T Griffith on USS Bowfin.png
gallery.source: RADM Ralph W Christie and LCDR Walter T Griffith on USS Bowfin
gallery.description: Rear Admiral Ralph Waldo Christie (left) and Lieutenant Commander Walter Thomas Griffith (right) on the cigarette deck of the submarine USS Bowfin (SS-287) during WWII. Christie joined the USS Bowfin partway through her third patrol and observed several attacks made by Griffith against Japanese shipping. Photo taken sometime between January 26 and February 2, 1944.
